text: Founded over 200 years ago by settlers fleeing the Lundayell Empire. They repaired an ancient airship and discovered the continent, cutting off contact with the Empire to start anew.
At the base of the Stormspire Peaks, by Lake Mirathorn, making it a strategic trade hub.
Approximately 30000 residents of diverse races, including humans, dwarves, elves, gnomes, halflings, dragonborn, and a sprinkling of goblins and bugbears.
Major industries include brewing, craftsmanship, fishing, agriculture, and magical goods. It's a key trade hub with access to rivers, mountain passes, and well-maintained roads.

Mirathorn is surrounded by ancient stone walls, built during the city's early days when threats were more frequent. The walls are tall and imposing, though they show signs of age and disuse, with ivy and moss creeping up their surfaces. Interspersed along the walls are guard towers, which now serve more as lookout points and symbolic reminders of the city's storied past than active defense posts. The main gates of Mirathorn are grand and sturdy, made of reinforced wood and iron. The gates are flanked by statues of the city's founders, looking both welcoming and protective.

The gates are heavily congested with people trying to enter the city. Guards manage the flow, checking goods and collecting tolls. The toll to enter the city is steep, designed to manage the influx and ensure only those with means can enter easily. The high toll has caused discontent among many visitors.

Outside the main gate, a group of Shepherd's Flock cultists is staging a protest. They are vocal and passionate, holding signs and chanting slogans against the toll, arguing it is unfair and exclusionary. The protest is led by charismatic cult leaders who stir up the crowd, encouraging them to demand entry without the toll. Some protesters are distributing pamphlets with their message, trying to gain more support. The city guards are visibly tense, trying to maintain order and prevent the protest from turning into a riot.

As the players approach Mirathorn, they are greeted by a vibrant and bustling scene of farmlands, workshops, and a diverse population on the move. The ancient city walls loom ahead, a testament to the city's rich history. The out town around the city is a chaotic but festive mix of tents and stalls, alive with the sounds and smells of a massive gathering. The main gates are a bottleneck of people and carts, with guards working diligently to manage the crowd. Amidst the throng, the players notice the protest by the Shepherd's Flock, adding a layer of tension and urgency to the scene. The high toll to enter the city is a point of contention, and the players may find themselves drawn into the unfolding drama as they navigate their way into Mirathorn for the Festival of Expansion.

document_title: Longmont Campaign GM Notes — Session 5 Prep
text: The Shepherd's Flock protest will escalate into a full riot during the Festival of Expansion closing ceremony. The cult leaders have been stockpiling weapons in carts disguised as merchant goods. City guards will be overwhelmed — this is the diversion.

document_title: Longmont Campaign GM Notes — Session 5 Prep
text: The merchant guild has planted a spy — Delara Windhaven — inside the city guard. She has been feeding guard rotation schedules to the cult. The players may discover her if they investigate the guard's unusual patrol gaps.

document_title: Longmont Campaign GM Notes — Session 5 Prep
text: Brother Ashwood, a Shepherd's Flock cell leader operating inside the city, will attempt to poison the main water supply during the closing ceremony while the riot draws attention to the gates. He carries a vial of slow-acting blight toxin. If not stopped, illness spreads through the lower districts within two days.

document_title: Session 6 Recap — The Road to Miraholm
text: Approaching Mirathorn they passed the abundance of the outskirts, a giant waterwheel visible from miles away against the mountain, the domineering walls around the city. Finally arriving at Outtown, the collection of shops, blacksmiths, breweries, tents, and temporary buildings erupting out of the city in preparation for the Festival of Expansion. After exploring a few shops, they decide it's time to head into the city and this 'toll' they heard folk grumbling about. Which is where they find a group gathering, passing out fliers chanting about how unfair the toll is. While they observe and chat with Captain Lysandra Ironveil, the crowd grows to around 50 people. The guards looking tense send a large contingent of troops out to disperse the crowd.

We find our heroes between guards and a large crowd attempting to start a riot over the toll to enter the gates. Stafl attempts to calm the crowd, however the crowd is already too loud to hear him. Caelynn then tells the crowd that we will talk to the Council about the fee if they settle down. Ephanna, working with the crowd, encourages the crowd to go to the Council themselves. Because of Caelynn the crowd opens and we are able to approach the Captain. The Captain allows us to cut the line to enter the city gates. Lyra, the leader of the crowd, and her followers leave to go back to their base.

Ephanna decides to take Torbin and go along with the Shepherd's Flock, wanting to help with their plans. Ephanna discovers that the group is called The Shepherds Flock. Each is wearing a symbol of their group and there is talk of their leader, The Shepherd, back in the Swamp to the north. Ephanna is captured, in a cell, bound and gagged. In the dim cell by the flickering of a torch there are three cages and on the end is someone standing over Torbin forcing him to eat some meat.
